issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a no-argument Milkable.messageOnMilk() method that returns a String (used as m.messageOnMilk()), but the solution repository defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) with a double parameter and implementations in Goat and Seal that require this parameter. This signature mismatch will cause confusion and compilation errors: students implementing the interfaces as described in the problem/template will find the solution's signatures different, and the solution code would not match the expected usage in the template Main (m.messageOnMilk()).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable interface and its implementations with the problem specification and template. Change the solution's Milkable interface to define String messageOnMilk() (no parameters), and update Seal and Goat to implement messageOnMilk() returning the specified format (e.g. "Seal Clarabelle is milked" / "Goat Buttinsky is milked"). Alternatively, if a volume parameter is intended pedagogically, update the problem statement and template usages to require and pass a double parameter to messageOnMilk(double volume). Prefer adjusting the solution to the no-arg signature to match the exercise description and template Main usage.

issues.description: The exercise text and template expect a Milkable.messageOnMilk() method with no parameters that returns a simple string like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (see problem statement and template Main usage). The solution, however, defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) (and Goat/Seal implement this signature), changing the method signature and the expected return format. This discrepancy breaks the one-to-one mapping between the problem requirements and the solution/template API: students following the specification will implement a no-argument messageOnMilk(), while the solution uses a different signature, causing compilation and conceptual mismatch and unnecessary cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the API across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem/template by updating Milkable to declare String messageOnMilk() (no parameters) and update Goat and Seal to implement messageOnMilk() returning "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"; or (B) modify the problem statement and template to require messageOnMilk(double volume) and update the textual specification to describe the volume-aware return format. Prefer option (A) to align with the original exercise description.
